runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current NPPF/town-centre PPG and adopted London Plan town-centre/retail policy with sequential, impact, hierarchy and local-demand tests kept proposal-specific.

sources.label: NPPF Section 7 town centres
sources.fact: Main town-centre uses should follow town-centre, edge-of-centre, then out-of-centre sequencing where relevant.

sources.label: NPPF retail/leisure impact test
sources.fact: Out-of-centre retail/leisure proposals not in accordance with an up-to-date plan require impact assessment above a locally-set threshold, or 2,500 square metres gross where none is set.

sources.label: GOV.UK Town centres and retail PPG
sources.fact: Current guidance supports a positive town-centre vision, structural-change evidence and mixed/complementary uses.

sources.label: Town-centre sequential test guidance
sources.fact: Applicant should demonstrate sequential-test compliance; failure to undertake a required sequential assessment can itself support refusal.

sources.label: Town-centre impact-test guidance
sources.fact: Impact assessment should be proportionate and consider vitality/viability and planned investment; passing it does not guarantee permission.

sources.label: London Plan Policy SD6
sources.fact: Adopted policy supports resilient, accessible, inclusive town centres/high streets and mixed-use/housing-led intensification where appropriate.

sources.label: London Plan Policy SD7
sources.fact: Boroughs should take a town-centres-first approach and apply sequential testing to relevant main town-centre uses.

sources.label: London Plan Policy SD8
sources.fact: Town-centre roles are managed through a London-wide network; diversification can be supported where commercial/retail demand declines.

sources.label: London Plan Policy SD9
sources.fact: Local partnership/implementation context supports town-centre objectives but is not a parcel development consent.

sources.label: London Plan Annex 1 Town Centre Network
sources.fact: Adopted annex classifies centres and identifies commercial/residential growth potential at network level.

sources.label: London Plan Policy E9 Retail
sources.fact: Retail planning should use strategic/local demand-and-supply evidence and manage surplus space, markets and mixed-use redevelopment.

sources.label: Current London Plan status
sources.fact: London Plan 2021 remains the adopted framework; current network and retail policies remain operative until formally superseded.

examples.result: Town-centre classification is not converted into automatic parcel development capacity.
Sequential-test applicability is checked against the actual proposed main town-centre use and location.
2,500 square metres is only the default retail/leisure impact threshold where no locally-set threshold applies.
Passing sequential/impact tests does not by itself guarantee permission.
Declining retail demand may support diversification but not automatic residential conversion of a candidate parcel.
Annex 1 growth potential remains network-level evidence, not a site-specific viability or capacity score.
E9 retail demand/supply evidence is not replaced with historic baseline floorspace assumptions.
No town-centre promotion occurs without exact site, use, hierarchy, availability and current local evidence.
